title: Themes and resources
sub: Fluent, light and dark, StaticResource and DynamicResource
cards/0/title: A theme is a set of styles for every control
cards/0/body:
App.axaml includes a theme, such as FluentTheme. It defines how every standard control looks.

A theme comes in variants: light and dark.
cards/1/q: RequestedThemeVariant="Default". Which theme will you get?
cards/1/options/0: Whatever the system uses: light or dark
cards/1/explain: Light or Dark must be set explicitly.
cards/2/body: Colors, brushes and sizes go into resources under a key, and you use them by key. Change it in one place, and it changes everywhere.
cards/3/body:
StaticResource looks up the resource once, at load time.
DynamicResource keeps watching it: if the resource changes (say, the theme switches), the element updates.

For theme-dependent colors, use DynamicResource.
cards/4/q: The user switched to the dark theme, but one button stayed light. What is the likely cause?
cards/4/options/0: Its color comes from StaticResource, which does not track changes
cards/4/options/2: The dark theme does not support buttons
cards/4/explain: DynamicResource would have updated along with the theme.
cards/5/title: A separate color for each theme
cards/5/body: You can define a resource separately for the light and dark themes with ThemeDictionaries.
cards/6/q: A background that changes along with the theme
cards/6/explain: StaticResource would grab the color only once.
cards/7/q: Match each term to what it does
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Light, dark or follow the system
cards/8/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/0: A theme defines the look of every standard control
cards/8/options/1: ThemeDictionaries set different values for Light and Dark
cards/8/options/2: DynamicResource updates when the theme changes
cards/8/options/3: A resource can be used in only one place
cards/8/explain: The whole point of a resource is to use it everywhere.
